episode_id: Catch up with upstream without losing what either side added, or reviving what either side removed. Start from upstream's dependency file and add back what I added./seed-5-lockfile_conflict-7516

reason: negative side failed: preconditions accepted 1 of 15 unrelated states (diverged seed 0 resolves to 'merge'); a precondition set that accepts unrelated states is a defect. It also accepted 1 more state(s) it must refuse: preconditions accepted 1 of 1 same-intent states (lockfile_conflict seed 2 resolves to 'keep_local', which accepts ['keep_local'], but the program implements 'take_upstream'); firing where a sibling resolution is correct is the mismatch this gate exists to refuse

refused_program.body:
git fetch {upstream_remote} || true
if ! git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  git merge --no-ff --no-commit {upstream_remote}/{upstream_branch} || true
fi
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U -z | tr '\0' '\n' > "$tmp/conflicts"
while IFS= read -r f; do
  [ -n "$f" ] || continue
  if ! git cat-file -e "MERGE_HEAD:$f" 2>/dev/null || ! git cat-file -e "HEAD:$f" 2>/dev/null; then
    git rm -f --ignore-unmatch -- "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1
    continue
  fi
  base=$(git merge-base HEAD MERGE_HEAD)
  git show "MERGE_HEAD:$f" > "$tmp/up"
  git show "HEAD:$f" > "$tmp/local"
  if git cat-file -e "$base:$f" 2>/dev/null; then
    git show "$base:$f" > "$tmp/base"
  else
    : > "$tmp/base"
  fi
  git diff --no-index -U0 "$tmp/base" "$tmp/local" > "$tmp/ldiff" 2>/dev/null || true
  awk '
    function flush(   i) {
      if (na > nd) for (i = nd + 1; i <= na; i++) print adds[i]
      na = 0; nd = 0
    }
    /^@@/ { flush(); next }
    /^\+\+\+/ { next }
    /^---/ { next }
    /^\+/ { adds[++na] = substr($0, 2); next }
    /^-/ { nd++; next }
    END { flush() }
  ' "$tmp/ldiff" > "$tmp/add"
  if [ -s "$tmp/add" ]; then
    grep -v '^$' "$tmp/up" > "$tmp/uppat" 2>/dev/null || true
    grep -vxF -f "$tmp/uppat" "$tmp/add" > "$tmp/add2" 2>/dev/null || true
    cat "$tmp/add2" > "$tmp/add"
  fi
  if [ -s "$tmp/add" ]; then
    anchor=$(ADD="$tmp/add" UP="$tmp/up" awk '
      FILENAME == ENVIRON["ADD"] { add[$0] = 1; next }
      FILENAME == ENVIRON["UP"] { up[$0] = 1; next }
      { L[++n] = $0 }
      END {
        last = 0
        for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (L[i] in add) last = i
        for (i = last + 1; i <= n; i++) if (L[i] in up) { print L[i]; exit }
      }' "$tmp/add" "$tmp/up" "$tmp/local")
    if [ -z "$anchor" ] && [ -s "$tmp/up" ]; then
      anchor=$(tail -n 1 "$tmp/up")
    fi
    ADD="$tmp/add" ANCHOR="$anchor" awk '
      FILENAME == ENVIRON["ADD"] { A[++na] = $0; next }
      {
        if (!done && ENVIRON["ANCHOR"] != "" && $0 == ENVIRON["ANCHOR"]) {
          for (i = 1; i <= na; i++) print A[i]
          done = 1
        }
        print
      }
      END { if (!done) for (i = 1; i <= na; i++) print A[i] }
    ' "$tmp/add" "$tmp/up" > "$tmp/merged"
  else
    cat "$tmp/up" > "$tmp/merged"
  fi
  cat "$tmp/merged" > "$f"
  git add -- "$f"
done < "$tmp/conflicts"
rm -rf "$tmp"
git commit -m "merge {upstream_remote}/{upstream_branch}: keep upstream deps and re-add local additions" || true
refused_program.intent: Catch up with upstream by merging it, resolving each conflicted file by starting from upstream's version and re-adding only the lines the local side inserted, so neither upstream-removed nor locally-removed content is revived, then committing the merge.
